notes.meaning: A long stretch of time passed, during which Saul also spent time in Arabia before returning to Damascus. His bold preaching proved that Jesus is the Messiah, which deeply frustrated the Jewish leaders. Because they could not defeat his arguments, they formed a plot to kill him.

Saul discovered the deadly plan his enemies had made against him. The Jewish leaders had guards posted at the city gates day and night to catch him as he tried to leave. Even though the danger was great, God kept Saul safe by making the plot known to him.

Under cover of darkness, local believers took Saul to an opening in the city wall. They placed him in a large basket and lowered him safely to the ground outside. Escaping danger in this way was not a lack of faith, but a wise way to preserve his life for future service.

When Saul arrived back in Jerusalem, he tried to join the fellowship of believers there. The Christians were terrified of him and doubted that he had truly become a follower of Jesus. They remembered how fiercely he had persecuted them and feared he was pretending in order to spy on them.

Barnabas showed great kindness and courage by taking Saul to Peter and James. He explained how the Lord Jesus had appeared and spoken to Saul on the road, and how boldly Saul had preached Christ in Damascus. This faithful testimony convinced the apostles that Saul's conversion was real.

Saul was welcomed into full fellowship and stayed with the believers in Jerusalem. He moved freely among them, sharing in their daily life and ministry. Everywhere he went, he spoke openly and courageously in the name of the Lord Jesus.

Saul shared the gospel and debated with Greek-speaking Jews in Jerusalem, just as Stephen had done before him. Because they could not answer his arguments, they became furious. Just like the leaders in Damascus, they began plotting to put him to death.

When the believers learned of the plot, they acted quickly to protect Saul. They escorted him down to the coastal city of Caesarea to get him out of harm's way. From there, they sent him by ship back to his hometown of Tarsus so he could minister in safety.

The churches throughout the whole region entered a time of rest and relief from persecution. Believers grew strong in their faith as they lived with deep reverence for God and enjoyed the comfort given by the Holy Spirit. As a result of this healthy spiritual life, many new people came to faith.

During this season of peace, Peter traveled through different towns to visit and strengthen the believers. The Bible calls these Christians 'saints,' meaning people set apart for God. His travels brought him to the town of Lydda to encourage the church there.

In Lydda, Peter met a man named Aeneas who had been paralyzed and confined to his bed for eight years. His condition was completely incurable by human medicine. This long illness showed how helpless the man was without divine help.

Peter told Aeneas that Jesus Christ was healing him right at that moment. He commanded him to get up and roll up his own mat, which proved that his strength was fully restored. Aeneas obeyed immediately and stood up completely healed by the power of Christ.

differ.view: Miracles of physical healing through individuals were special signs given to confirm the apostles' message during the foundation of the church.
God continues to perform miraculous healings through believers today as the Holy Spirit directs.

notes.meaning: The people living in Lydda and across the fertile plain of Sharon saw Aeneas walking and healthy. Because they knew how long he had been bedridden, they recognized God's hand in his recovery. This visible proof of Christ's power led a great number of people to turn to the Lord in faith.

In the nearby seaport of Joppa, there was a devoted female disciple named Tabitha, which translates to Dorcas in Greek, meaning 'gazelle.' She lived out her faith in practical ways every day. She was well known for constantly doing good deeds and giving help to the poor.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Tabitha is honored as a holy widow whose life of charity and service set a lasting example for the church.

notes.meaning: During this time, Tabitha became very ill and died, causing deep grief among the believers. Following Jewish burial customs, they washed her body with care to prepare her for interment. Instead of burying her right away, they placed her body in an upstairs room.

Joppa was only about six miles from Lydda, and the believers heard that Peter was there. They sent two messengers with an urgent plea for him to come without delay. They looked to him for comfort in their sorrow, and some may have hoped God would work a miracle through him.

Peter went with the two men and was taken upstairs to the room where Tabitha lay. A group of poor widows gathered around him in tears, showing him the robes and shirts Dorcas had sewn for them while she was alive. Their gratitude showed how deeply her acts of love had touched their lives.

Peter asked everyone to leave the room so he could seek God in quiet prayer. He knelt down to pray, acknowledging that only the Lord has power over death, and then told Tabitha to get up. At his command, she opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up alive.

Peter reached out his hand and helped Tabitha stand up on her feet. Then he called the believers and the weeping widows back into the room and presented her alive. Her return from death brought immense joy and relieved the poverty of those she cared for.

The news of Tabitha being raised to life spread rapidly through the entire city of Joppa. The miracle was not just an act of kindness, but a sign that confirmed the gospel message. As people heard about it, many put their trust in the Lord Jesus.

Peter remained in Joppa for many days, taking time to teach and establish the new believers in their faith. He chose to lodge with a man named Simon, who worked as a tanner preparing animal skins. Because strict Jewish traditions treated tanning as an unclean trade, Peter's stay showed his humble spirit and prepared him to cross old cultural boundaries.
